- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.2), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is trending up.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days); apply a 1-2 day lag correction or dampen momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is 2-3σ above recent mean, reduce by 5-10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; add 1-2 days of “tail risk” adjustment if sentiment is volatile or bullish.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.8) and price is trending, model tends to lag; forecast should be 1-2 days ahead of true trend.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes; use 3-5 day rolling average of sentiment to filter noise.
